surface: Goals typography and physical action controls
scope: Correct the approved living-commitment direction where live type and nested app-style buttons still detach from the room; rebuild the returning action as one tappable quest folio, then carry the same type and latch language through hard-day, support, Goal Detail, opening, and arrival states without changing the product journey
user_job: Recognize the one goal and exact next Quest immediately, then begin or choose a gentler route through controls that feel physically native to the room

active_sources.judged_state: One personal goal at the desk with an exact first action and visibly secondary lighter route
The exact plan is registered to the lit arch and crossing it is a clear, real action

product.decision: Keep the approved action-first journey unchanged: one focus goal, one exact next Quest, one lighter route, and direct exact-Quest handoff
product.proof: The returning, hard-day, opening, support, and detail journeys retain their exact callbacks, persistence, and Quest identity

interaction.decision: The quest folio itself becomes the touch target and its attached latch acknowledges immediately, enters a truthful opening state, and rejects rapid re-entry
interaction.proof: Rest, pointer-down, accepted, transition, back, and rapid-repeat states remain observable through the existing semantic keys

visual.decision: One photographed-room type system and one physical folio/latch control replace the nested dark card plus shiny rounded button; Fraunces owns meaning, EB Garamond owns physical labels and latches, and Inter is reserved for explanatory copy
visual.proof: Fresh same-state renders show one action surface, fewer type voices, no detached gold slab, and clear hierarchy over the room at modern-iPhone size

anti_fallbacks.fallback: Another contrast, gradient, shadow, or radius tweak to the existing nested card and button
anti_fallbacks.why: The visible defect is the component relationship and type-role drift, not insufficient decoration

anti_fallbacks.fallback: A flat text link that removes the one clear action
anti_fallbacks.why: The action must remain obvious, tactile, and attached to a physical surface

anti_fallbacks.fallback: A different control language for hard-day, support, detail, and opening states
anti_fallbacks.why: The correction only succeeds if the room remembers the same material and typography across the journey

first_real_slice.scenario: Return to an active HOME goal with one exact due Quest and one lighter route
first_real_slice.real_inputs: The production-equivalent calm-apartment goal, Clear the kitchen counter Quest, saved reason, lighter action, and return evidence
first_real_slice.user_action: Read the focus, press the unified Quest folio, and follow the room transition
first_real_slice.expected_outcome: The exact Quest is the first read, the whole folio acknowledges the hand, its latch resolves locally, and the room journey opens the same Quest
first_real_slice.state_boundary: The callback, hero identity, rapid-entry guard, and exact Quest handoff remain unchanged

required_states.state: Returning goal and quest folio parked over the apartment
required_states.why_can_disprove: The folio can still look like a generic card or the type can remain noisier than the room
A full-surface control can lose immediate causality or make the pending state jump

required_states.state: The exact Quest named after the room crossing
required_states.why_can_disprove: The new type language can break continuity if arrival reverts to floating all-caps UI

ripple_map.state: No due Quest and a saved fallback action
ripple_map.expected_effect: The same folio changes copy and pigment without becoming a separate green UI treatment
ripple_map.verification_plan: Render and inspect the hard-day golden and activate the fallback

ripple_map.surface_or_primitive: Goal Detail current action and supporting controls
ripple_map.state: Proof, return plan, linked Quests, add Quest, and release controls
ripple_map.expected_effect: The current action is the same folio and secondary controls use one quiet physical label language
ripple_map.verification_plan: Render default and 2x detail states and exercise action/add/release behavior

ripple_map.expected_effect: One attached drawer row replaces the generic accordion and circular tile badges
ripple_map.verification_plan: Render collapsed and expanded states and activate both choices

ripple_map.surface_or_primitive: One-time opening clasps, threshold, and Quest arrival copy
ripple_map.state: Desk, threshold, arrival, Reduced Motion, and modern-iPhone text scale
ripple_map.expected_effect: Compact latches and sentence-case environmental copy remain one family with the returning folio
ripple_map.verification_plan: Recapture the opening and returning motion stories and inspect adjacent frames

unverified_property: Whether the unified folio and expanded EB Garamond physical-label role actually feel authored with the room instead of merely cleaner in code

decisive_check.method: Render the returning, pressed, accepted, hard-day, support-open, Goal Detail, opening, and arrival states and compare the approved target and prior build beside the new build
decisive_check.target: 402x874 modern-iPhone review plus 430x932 compatibility and focused motion keyframes
decisive_check.pass_condition: The room stays the world, the exact Quest owns the first action read, no nested gold slab remains, secondary controls stop competing, and the same type/material logic survives every adjacent state
